feed.title: The SpaceX Dispatch
feed.subtitle: Weekday briefing on SpaceX launches, Starlink, AI and the SPCX stock
feed.rights: The SpaceX Dispatch is an independent weekday digest of public news, X posts, regulatory filings and market data about Space Exploration Technologies Corp., and is not affiliated with the company. Quotes are verbatim; emoji in quoted posts are omitted for print. Market data are delayed and may be revised. Not investment advice.

entry.title: Thursday, November 12, 2026: USSF-627 flies; the double catch is a day away
entry.summary:
A Falcon 9 lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base at 11:36 p.m. EST Wednesday with the classified USSF-627 mission for the U.S. Space Force, two days after its first target date, and its booster landed on a droneship in the Pacific, SpaceX posted. At Starbase, the 26 Starlink satellites for Starship Flight 15 were rolled out to Ship 42, and airspace closures went up for Friday's 5:45 p.m. EST launch and Saturday's planned ship catch.

The Space Development Agency (SDA) is paying SpaceX $9.9 million to study its Starlink laser terminal for missile-tracking satellites, and Ookla found that Starlink is winning city customers faster than rural ones. SPCX fell 2.33% as Wall Street rallied, on the day a secondhand report said Anthropic would not renew its compute contract with SpaceX.

entry.title: Wednesday, November 11, 2026: A squeeze test at catch height
entry.summary:
Booster 22, the first Super Heavy V3 booster meant to return to the launch site for a catch, rolled to the pad at Starbase and was held aloft by the tower's arms for a "suspended squeeze test at catch height," SpaceX posted Tuesday at 1:21 p.m. EST. Starship Flight 15 still targets Friday at 5:45 p.m. EST, pending regulatory approval, and airspace notices for the launch went up Wednesday morning.

Off the pad, SpaceX signed a deal with Germany's SINGULUS for a solar-cell production line to power its Starmind satellites, and the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) opened its review of SpaceX's purchase of nationwide 800 MHz spectrum. USSF-627 slipped a second time, to tonight, and SPCX rose 0.72%.

entry.title: Tuesday, November 10, 2026: "Fundamentally an infrastructure company"
entry.summary:
"Yes, we are a rocket company, but fundamentally we are an infrastructure company at this point," SpaceX vice president of launch Kiko Dontchev said at last week's UP.Summit, Ars Technica reported Monday. He said Grok now finds debris in rocket parts better than human inspectors, that Falcon 9 is headed for retirement and that Starship's Florida pad is "effectively complete."

Starship Flight 15 is now on the Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) operations advisory for Friday at 5:45 p.m. EST, with Booster 22 lifted onto Pad 2 late Monday. USSF-627 slipped a day to tonight, and SPCX gained 5.81% Monday in a broad market rally.

entry.title: Monday, November 9, 2026: A double catch on Friday the 13th
entry.summary:
SpaceX is targeting Friday, Nov. 13, for Starship Flight 15, with a 75-minute window opening at 5:45 p.m. EST, pending regulatory approval, according to SpaceX's mission page. The plan is to catch both the Super Heavy booster and, for the first time, the Starship upper stage at the Starbase tower. "If both are successful, it will mark the first time that all parts of an orbital rocket return to Earth intact," Musk posted at 10:47 a.m. EST Friday.

Over the weekend, Falcon 9 flew USSF-432 from California, an 8-K confirmed that Alphabet's Donald Harrison left the board, and SPCX recovered most of Thursday's drop.

entry.title: Friday, November 6, 2026: Starlink for Indonesian schools and clinics
entry.summary:
Musk amplified two Starlink stories from Indonesia: "Starlink saves lives," he posted at 11:36 a.m. EST Thursday, and "Starlink enables education in remote areas" at 4:32 a.m. EST Friday. Katingan Regency's local government is distributing Starlink kits to schools and clinics, according to official Diskominfostandi notices.

The same coverage window ends with Falcon 9 USSF-432 set for tonight from Vandenberg and SPCX's sharpest one-day drop since listing.

entry.title: Thursday, November 5, 2026: Free Standard kits for early Starlink customers
entry.summary:
"Free new dish for all early Starlink customers," Musk posted at 10:02 a.m. EST Wednesday, quoting a report that Starlink is rolling out free upgrades for its earliest users still on first-generation kits. Eligible customers "can receive a new Standard kit at no cost," with a free mount and optional free installation, according to Starlink support language quoted by Sawyer Merritt and confirmed by Musk.

The confirmation came the same day SpaceX and Qualcomm detailed Dragonwing 64T64R radios for Starlink Mobile's terrestrial 5G build, and a day before Falcon 9 is due to loft USSF-432 from Vandenberg.

entry.title: Wednesday, November 4, 2026: Morgan Stanley nearly doubles its 2027 forecast
entry.summary:
Morgan Stanley analyst Adam Jonas now expects SpaceX to generate $175 billion in revenue in 2027 and $289 billion in 2028, increases of 93% and 84% from his previous forecasts, Investing.com reported Wednesday. His 2028 operating income estimate rose 72% to $119 billion, and the bank now sees SpaceX turning free-cash-flow positive in 2031 instead of 2035, with cumulative external borrowing of about $390 billion rather than $670 billion.

At roughly $140 a share and a $1.91 trillion market value, SpaceX trades at 17.6 times projected 2028 adjusted earnings, Jonas calculates, slightly below the bank's 17.7 times for the S&P 500. His $300 target implies about 114% upside. In his model the space and connectivity businesses account for about $123 of the share price, leaving $17 for AI (Investing.com). Jonas expects earnings to grow about 150% a year from 2026 to 2030. The shares still fell about 5% early Wednesday after the midterm elections.

entry.title: Tuesday, November 3, 2026: "Boost it": Isaacman on Hubble's future
entry.summary:
"Hubble, you can't let it have an uncontrolled re-entry. That would not be the right thing to do. If you're going to spend money to go up there and do something, you might as well boost it, get as much science as you possibly can out of it," NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman told NASASpaceflight in an interview published Tuesday.

NASA issued a Request for Information on Oct. 29 asking companies whether they could boost Hubble to a higher orbit, service it to enhance its capabilities, or carry out a controlled re-entry or disposal, NASA said. Responses are due by 3 p.m. EST on Monday, Nov. 30. Hubble has no propulsion of its own and is likely to re-enter in 2033 or 2034, so a mission would need to fly by 2032, the agency said.

entry.title: Monday, November 2, 2026: SpaceX in talks for Boost Mobile
entry.summary:
SpaceX is in talks to buy EchoStar's wireless service Boost Mobile or gain access to its network, which EchoStar leases from AT&T and T-Mobile, The Washington Post reported Monday, citing people familiar with the negotiations. The talks have run for months and are about launching SpaceX's own wireless service through a deal with EchoStar, Reuters wrote, summarizing the report.

The goal is a hybrid satellite-and-ground network under the Starlink Mobile name to compete with AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile (Reuters). Musk approached the heads of the top U.S. telecom companies, including Verizon, in recent months to ask for access to their networks, according to The Washington Post, which called a deal "a potential back door into the $235 billion wireless market." SpaceX and EchoStar did not immediately respond to requests for comment from Reuters.

entry.title: Friday, October 30, 2026: FCC proposes 482 MHz more for satellite-to-phone service
entry.summary:
The Federal Communications Commission on Thursday voted to propose making an additional 482 megahertz of spectrum available for Supplemental Coverage from Space, the satellite-to-phone service behind Starlink Mobile, expanding the eligible bands from five to 13 (FCC). The proposal would also eliminate the rule's leasing requirements and its geographically independent area requirement, replacing them with flexible license areas and coexistence agreements between satellite operators and carriers, and seeks comment on direct-to-device performance requirements. "With today's proposal, we take our most comprehensive step yet to modernize the FCC's rules for direct-to-device," Chairman Brendan Carr said, according to the FCC.

It is a notice of proposed rulemaking: the next step is public comment, and final rules would need another vote. AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile had wanted 290 MHz cut from the plan, Teslarati posted. "Streamlining rules and ensuring access to critical radio frequency (RF) resources are more important than ever," said Tom Stroup, president of the Satellite Industry Association (SIA).

entry.title: Thursday, October 29, 2026: Musk: Ship 42 will be the first ship caught by the tower
entry.summary:
"Ship 42 static fires complete," SpaceX posted at 12:10 p.m. EDT Wednesday. "The Starship preparing for Flight 15 performed a full duration, six-engine static fire, and fired a single Raptor engine to simulate a deorbit burn." Quoting the post at 10:37 p.m., Elon Musk wrote: "As the prophecy foretold, Starship 42 will be the first tower catch."

Ship 42 left the Massey's test site that night and was moved along Highway 4 back to the production site, Tracking The Starbase posted at 11:15 p.m., and was "back in the barn" by 2:01 a.m. Thursday (post). SpaceX has not announced a date for Flight 15, which Launch Library 2 lists for no earlier than November from Pad 2 at Starbase.

entry.title: Wednesday, October 28, 2026: SpaceX tells the FAA it wants 10,000 launches a year
entry.summary:
SpaceX told federal aviation regulators that it anticipates conducting 10,000 launches a year itself, and that the Federal Aviation Administration's air traffic control structure and processes, not rockets, are what stand in the way, TeslaNorth reported. The comments answer a Department of Transportation and FAA request for information on where to site new spaceports and how to give critical launch corridors priority in U.S. airspace, filed in docket FAA-2026-9736, whose comment window closed on October 26. The FAA's own August 25 notice forecast about 10,000 licensed launches and reentries a year by 2035; SpaceX put today's level at 182 licensed launches and 7 licensed reentries in 2025 (TeslaNorth).

"10k Starship launches/year is just from Starbase Louisiana," Elon Musk posted at 2:07 a.m. EDT Wednesday, quoting a summary of the filing. According to the filing, the planned Louisiana spaceport is designed for about 30 launches and reentries per day (Benzinga, Stocktwits). To a user who wrote that SpaceX "rewrites aviation control software to launch more," Musk replied at 3:58 a.m.: "We address the limiting factor."

SpaceX pointed to Cleared, its real-time launch-status and airspace platform, which it said most major U.S. airlines already use at no cost along with its API, and asked that such data be built into FAA flow-management and controller tools so hazard areas can shrink and move with the vehicle instead of closing large blocks of sky for long windows. None of the filings approves any launches: licensing, environmental review and air-traffic integration still have to follow (TeslaNorth).

entry.title: Tuesday, October 27, 2026: Starlink Mobile goes live in Brazil
entry.summary:
"Starlink Mobile is now live in Brazil with @vivobr! 50M customers can use apps and messaging in cellular dead zones — with 7M phones already connected. This is the first nationwide service to cover the entire country," Starlink posted at 11:53 a.m. EDT Monday. Michael Nicolls shared the announcement: "Starlink Mobile in Brazil with @vivobr !"

Vivo calls the service Vivo Satélite. Customers on eligible plans can use messaging apps, maps and the carrier's support channel where there is no tower signal, without the data counting against their monthly allowance, and the service is free for a limited time, O Globo reported. Video calls and general web browsing stay blocked. No sign-up or app is needed: the phone must support LTE or 5G, run the latest software and have data roaming switched on, and it needs a clear view of the sky.

The link runs in the 2.5 GHz band at up to 100 watts of transmit power. Brazil's telecom regulator, Anatel, set up a supervised test regime in June, and the authorization has been renewed to April 22, 2029, with commercial use allowed under the experimental rules (O Globo).

entry.title: Monday, October 26, 2026: A $40 billion lease for GPUs
entry.summary:
SpaceX has signed a binding commitment letter for a master finance lease of about $40 billion with an entity managed by Apollo, under which the lessor buys pods of graphics processing units (GPUs) and leases them to SpaceX, according to an 8-K accepted by the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) at 8:00 a.m. EDT Monday. The letter was signed on Saturday, October 24. Each lease schedule runs about five to five and a quarter years, with rent paid quarterly in advance: one-twentieth of the financed cost plus a fixed annual rate and costs. Closing is expected before the end of the year, and schedules begin in the first half of 2027 as the hardware is delivered.

Elon Musk had previewed the deal on Sunday. "SpaceX closed $40B of debt for GPUs, but we're investment grade and have Starlink & launch revenue," he posted at 3:11 p.m. EDT, and half an hour later added that it is "primarily callable debt for GPU purchases that will arrive in Q1 and Q2. Not a major factor this quarter." CNBC reported the filing Monday morning. SPCX rose 1.89% on Friday to $147.49.

entry.title: Friday, October 23, 2026: A 9.1% drop as the first lock-up opens
entry.summary:
SPCX fell 9.14% to $144.75 on Thursday, on 195 million shares, about twice its 30-session average, giving back all of Wednesday's 7.79% gain and more. The slide "followed profit-taking and a share unlock," The Motley Fool wrote; under the prospectus, up to 1.3 billion locked-up Class A shares could be sold from Thursday, with up to 328.4 million more from Saturday. The Nasdaq 100 lost 2.90% and the S&P 500 1.21%.

After the close, SpaceX filed its third-quarter 10-Q, which puts the Tesla talks in writing: "our board of directors has formed a special committee to evaluate a potential combination between SpaceX and Tesla, Inc.," and "No determination by our special committee has been made." Starlink 15-15, scrubbed a third straight day on Thursday, tries again this evening.

entry.title: Thursday, October 22, 2026: A 7.8% jump, and a lock-up opens
entry.summary:
SPCX closed up 7.79% at $159.31 on Wednesday, on 219 million shares, more than twice its 30-session average, after SpaceX "posted its first profit as a public company," Reuters reported. Analysts lifted price targets across the board; JPMorgan's Doug Anmuth more than doubled his to $500, writing that "SpaceX's ambitions are bigger than any company's we've seen," CNBC reported.

From Thursday, up to 1.3 billion locked-up Class A shares, 28% of those under the 180-day lock-up, can be sold, followed by up to 328.4 million on Saturday and the rest on December 8, under the prospectus. A Starlink launch from California was scrubbed for weather Wednesday evening and tries again tonight.

entry.title: Wednesday, October 21, 2026: Revenue up 161% as AI becomes the biggest business
entry.summary:
SpaceX reported third-quarter revenue of $14.58 billion, against the $12.72 billion analysts expected, and net income of $4.4 billion, compared with a $1.1 billion loss a year earlier, Reuters reported. The Super Intelligence (SI) segment brought in $7.6 billion, more than Starlink and launch combined, according to the company's results release.

"We are in an inflection moment for SpaceX across launch, connectivity and superintelligence," Musk said on the call. SPCX, which closed down 0.11% at $147.79 on Tuesday, rose 4.6% after hours, Bloomberg Law reported. That evening, a Starlink launch from California was scrubbed for a technical issue.

entry.title: Tuesday, October 20, 2026: Starfall flies again on results day
entry.summary:
A Falcon 9 lifted off from Cape Canaveral at 7:04 a.m. EDT Tuesday with Bandwagon-5, a rideshare of 32 payloads that includes the second flight of SpaceX's Starfall return capsule, a day late because of recovery weather. The booster landed on the drone ship A Shortfall of Gravitas, and payload deployments began about an hour after launch (SpaceX).

After the close, SpaceX reports its third quarter, its second report as a public company. Musk's pledged share for every American child will go through Trump Accounts, President Trump said Monday, The Verge reported. SPCX rose 1.32% to $147.96 on Monday.

entry.title: Monday, October 19, 2026: Results tomorrow, and a share for every child
entry.summary:
SpaceX reports its third quarter after the close on Tuesday, its second report as a public company, and up to 1.3 billion locked-up shares become sellable two trading days later. "Next year, I will give one of my SpaceX shares to every kid in America. This will be the first of many," Elon Musk posted at 3:52 a.m. EDT Monday, a gift worth about $10.5 billion at Friday's close, CNBC calculated.

Bandwagon-5 slipped a day to Tuesday because of recovery weather. New York City Council members called SpaceXAI's testimony on Grok safety evasive, and Ukraine's president blamed Washington for Starshield speed limits. SPCX fell 1.74% to $146.03 on Friday.

entry.title: Friday, October 16, 2026: USSF-481 flies, Dragon docks, and SpaceX lends Tesla its thrusters
entry.summary:
A Falcon 9 launched the classified USSF-481 mission from Vandenberg at 8:01 p.m. EDT Thursday, 17 minutes into its window, and the booster landed on its 28th flight, Spaceflight Now reported. An hour later, at a SpaceX test site in McGregor, Texas, Tesla's new Roadster flew on SpaceX cold-gas thrusters. "Tesla x SpaceX," Elon Musk posted.

Cargo Dragon docked at the space station Thursday morning. Ukraine says its Starlink and Starshield service is back to full capacity. Musk says the Star Mind orbital computer SpaceX is building with Nvidia reaches volume production next year, and SpaceXAI testifies to the New York City Council at 10 a.m. EDT today. SPCX fell 2.33% to $148.62.

entry.title: Thursday, October 15, 2026: A Starshield speed limit hits Ukraine's front line; Musk says Washington decides
entry.summary:
Ukrainian officials said military Starshield terminals were restricted while moving overnight into Wednesday, slowing drones and ground robots. "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS," Elon Musk replied to Ukraine's Mykhailo Fedorov, who had said connectivity at up to 160 km/h was being restored.

Cargo Dragon is due to dock at the International Space Station (ISS) at about 11 a.m. EDT today, and a Falcon 9 is scheduled to launch the USSF-481 mission from California at 7:44 p.m. EDT. SPCX fell 2.80% to $152.16 as a hot inflation report hit AI-linked stocks. There were no new SEC filings.

entry.title: Wednesday, October 14, 2026: FAA opens a full environmental review of 456 Starship launches a year from Starbase
entry.summary:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) published a notice today that it will prepare a programmatic environmental impact statement on SpaceX's plan to raise Starship operations at Starbase, Texas, to as many as 456 launches and 912 landings a year, from 25 launches today. Public scoping meetings are set for November 17 to 19, with comments due November 30. SPCX fell 4.21% to $156.54 on Tuesday, the day the plan became public.

Ship 40, the first Starship to come back to its launch site after flying, now stands in a Megabay, where SpaceX says it will yield "first-of-its-kind data" on a flown heatshield. Cargo Dragon is due at the space station Thursday, the same evening a Falcon 9 is scheduled to launch USSF-481. SpaceXAI agreed to testify before the New York City Council on Friday. There were no new SEC filings.

entry.title: Tuesday, October 13, 2026: Two Falcon 9s in ten hours: Starlink from California, then cargo Dragon to the station
entry.summary:
Falcon 9 launched 27 Starlink satellites from Vandenberg at 8:28 p.m. EDT Monday, the first Falcon 9 Starlink mission since September 19, and then sent NASA's 35th cargo Dragon (CRS-35) toward the International Space Station (ISS) from Cape Canaveral at 6:33 a.m. EDT today. Dragon is due to dock on Thursday at about 11 a.m. EDT; its booster landed at Landing Zone 40. A Bandwagon-5 rideshare is now dated for Monday, October 19.

SpaceX's AI arm unified Grok, Cursor and X Premium into one five-tier plan, The X Subscription. Poland said two Turkish citizens were arrested in Germany over a fire at a Starlink ground station that Warsaw blames on Russian intelligence. India's communications ministry called complaints about Starlink's wait "baseless." SPCX rose 0.52% to $163.42. There were no new SEC or FAA filings.

entry.title: Monday, October 12, 2026: The SDA satellites fly, and Musk puts a ship catch on Starship's next flight
entry.summary:
A Falcon 9 finally launched 21 Space Development Agency (SDA) data-relay satellites from California early Saturday, five days after an automatic abort, and its booster landed back at Vandenberg. Two more Falcon 9s are lined up: Starlink 15-25 on Monday evening, after slipping from Saturday and Sunday, and the CRS-35 cargo Dragon to the International Space Station (ISS) at 6:33 a.m. EDT Tuesday.

Speaking by video at a Tesla fan event in Texas on Saturday, Elon Musk said Starship Flight 15, "hopefully" four to six weeks away, will try to catch the ship with the launch tower. Starlink won a full operating license in Venezuela and offered free service in quake-hit Panama, while Musk escalated his fight with Mukesh Ambani over India. SPCX rose 1.25% Friday to $162.57 as Barclays started coverage at Overweight. SpaceX has filed nothing new with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) since Friday morning.

entry.title: Friday, October 9, 2026: SpaceX buys its way into the phone business, and carrier stocks take the hit
entry.summary:
After the market closed on Thursday, SpaceX said it will buy Grain Management's nationwide 800 MHz spectrum portfolio, up to 14 megahertz of paired low-band airwaves that it says will let Starlink Mobile "become a major mobile carrier in the US." The price was not disclosed; The Wall Street Journal reported about $8 billion in cash. The deal still needs approval from the Federal Communications Commission (FCC). By Friday morning, shares of AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile were down 5.5% to 7.4% before the open, Reuters reported.

The news came too late to help SPCX, which fell 4.19% to $160.57 during Thursday's session, its second straight loss, before rising about 2.5% in extended trading. Up to 328.4 million more Class A shares become free to sell from Friday under the IPO lock-up schedule. Crew-12 is home after Thursday's splashdown. Next on the launch schedule: a Space Development Agency (SDA) mission early Saturday and the CRS-35 cargo flight on Tuesday. SpaceX has filed nothing new with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) since Thursday morning.

entry.title: Thursday, October 8, 2026: Crew-12 splashes down, Starlink signs up whole airlines, and Elon Musk takes his India fight public
entry.summary:
The Dragon capsule Freedom splashed down off Los Angeles at 11:34 a.m. EDT Thursday, bringing four Crew-12 astronauts home after 237 days at the International Space Station (ISS). Starlink had a strong day with airlines: American Airlines will put it on its entire mainline fleet of more than 1,000 jets, KLM will offer it free on long-haul flights from mid-2027, and Royal Air Maroc became the first African airline to sign on.

In India, Elon Musk accused "certain oligarchs" of blocking Starlink's license, and the government called the claim baseless. On Wall Street, a report that SpaceX is seeking about $40 billion of debt to buy Nvidia chips helped push SPCX down 2.51% to $167.60 on Wednesday, ending a three-day run. In Washington, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) put two direct-to-device spectrum proposals on its October 29 agenda. SpaceX has filed nothing new with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) since Wednesday morning.
